method: Bounded Family landscape; source identities checked via PubMed. Not a systematic review per Driver.

CUL-F01.constructs: Shared value prominence is a cultural aggregate, not an individual's value score.
CUL-F01.mechanisms: Transmission, selection and institutions can stabilize shared priorities.
CUL-F01.operations: Value framing or salience manipulations measure individual responses, not immediate cultural change.
CUL-F01.measurement: Aggregation, measurement invariance and referent specification are required.
CUL-F01.boundaries: Cross-national mean differences do not identify causal value effects.

CUL-F02.constructs: Autonomous, interdependent, relational and collective selfhood models differ from individual self-construal.
CUL-F02.mechanisms: Socialization and institutions may sustain agency norms over time.
CUL-F02.operations: Priming an individual self-description does not manipulate population prevalence.
CUL-F02.measurement: Level and referent must be explicit.
CUL-F02.boundaries: State primes cannot establish durable shared models.

CUL-F03.constructs: Tightness, deviance tolerance, entrenchment, scope and content-specific norms are distinct.
CUL-F03.mechanisms: Sanctioning and coordination can stabilize norms under threat.
CUL-F03.operations: Threat or constraint primes are not equivalent to a culture-level tightness intervention.
CUL-F03.measurement: Multi-level surveys and behavioral sanctions measure different components.
CUL-F03.boundaries: Country association, individual perception and shared norm must not be collapsed.

CUL-F04.constructs: Honor, face, dignity, hierarchy, prestige and reputation-defense obligations are related but non-identical.
CUL-F04.operations: Insult experiments expose a person to provocation; they do not manipulate culture-level honor strength.
CUL-F04.measurement: Regional comparison and physiological/aggressive responses require level separation.
CUL-F04.boundaries: Selection, gender and regional transfer limit causal inference.

CUL-F05.constructs: Kinship, filial, lineage, family, hospitality and resource-sharing obligations require a specified referent.
CUL-F05.mechanisms: Socialization and sanctioning may transmit obligations.
CUL-F05.operations: No single family vignette changes a shared cultural obligation.
CUL-F05.measurement: Individual endorsement differs from community prevalence.
CUL-F05.boundaries: Household and society levels cannot be inferred from one another.

CUL-F06.constructs: Conformist, prestige, success, elder and vertical transmission are mechanisms, not observed outcomes alone.
CUL-F06.mechanisms: Learning biases can affect diffusion conditional on networks and payoffs.
CUL-F06.operations: Model exposure packages often vary source status and content together.
CUL-F06.measurement: Transmission fidelity requires repeated measures and content identity.
CUL-F06.boundaries: Laboratory copying is not population-level cultural persistence.

CUL-F07.constructs: Collective memory, narrative centrality, schema consensus and symbolic meaning span individual and collective levels.
CUL-F07.mechanisms: Narratives can organize identity and recall through repeated social practice.
CUL-F07.operations: Narrative exposure is not collective-memory change without shared uptake.
CUL-F07.measurement: Recall, narrative endorsement and archival prevalence are distinct.
CUL-F07.boundaries: Reviews are theoretical context, not experimental evidence of a specific edge.

CUL-F08.constructs: Ritual expectation, significance, cost, synchronization and custom entrenchment are distinct.
CUL-F08.mechanisms: Coordinated action can affect individual cohesion while ritual institutions persist at group level.
CUL-F08.operations: Synchrony, exertion, music and arousal are often bundled.
CUL-F08.measurement: Behavioral synchrony does not itself measure a cultural synchronization norm.
CUL-F08.boundaries: Social closeness/cooperation findings do not establish cultural Driver change.

CUL-F09.constructs: Sacred commitment, taboo, purity, moralization, boundary rigidity and violence legitimacy are distinct.
CUL-F09.mechanisms: Moralization and sanctions may protect symbolic boundaries.
CUL-F09.operations: Sacred-value elicitation is measurement, not a direct culture-level manipulation.
CUL-F09.measurement: Individual conviction differs from shared prevalence.
CUL-F09.boundaries: No universal pathway from sacredness to violence is inferred.

CUL-F10.constructs: Ideal affect, expression legitimacy, display rules, restraint and shame regulation differ.
CUL-F10.mechanisms: Social learning and anticipated sanctions shape expression.
CUL-F10.operations: Emotion induction does not manipulate the display rule itself.
CUL-F10.measurement: Reported emotion, expression and perceived norm require separate measures.
CUL-F10.boundaries: State emotion cannot stand for cultural convention.

CUL-F11.constructs: Attention, dialectical reasoning, causal explanation, epistemic authority, future orientation and fatalism differ.
CUL-F11.mechanisms: Institutions and learned conventions may shape knowledge practices.
CUL-F11.operations: Task performance is not prevalence of a cultural convention.
CUL-F11.measurement: Cross-language task differences require invariance and exposure controls.
CUL-F11.boundaries: Cognitive style and culture-level convention remain separate.

CUL-F12.constructs: Directness, explicitness, politeness, honorifics, euphemism and silence norms are separate message conventions.
CUL-F12.mechanisms: Audience design and sanctions condition communication choices.
CUL-F12.operations: Wording manipulation changes a message, not necessarily a cultural convention.
CUL-F12.measurement: Message feature, speaker behavior and shared norm must be separated.
CUL-F12.boundaries: Prior Informational review is reused for euphemism-to-metaphor scope.

CUL-F13.constructs: Identity narrative, prototype, boundary, assimilation, accommodation, heritage, reconciliation and generational distance differ.
CUL-F13.mechanisms: Institutions and discourse can shape individual endorsement over time, but shared norms require aggregation.
CUL-F13.operations: Multiculturalism framing can shift individual evaluation; it does not directly establish culture-level accommodation norm strength.
CUL-F13.measurement: Individual attitude, group identification and collective prevalence require distinct measures.
CUL-F13.boundaries: Generational distance needs a versioned profile and distance metric before causal-source use.
